A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VocADT study and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables and appendices. Existing content can be matched despite the expanded and reorganized appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original multilingual vocabulary-adaptation and downstream translation experiments, including language-level results in Tables 2–8 and grouping and auxiliary-loss analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds experiments with a unified 11-language vocabulary, LLaMA2-7B and additional auxiliary-loss settings.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same adapter matrices, frozen original weights, initialization rules, auxiliary loss and embedding-merging procedure. The subsequent ALMA fine-tuning procedure is also unchanged. The additional experiments reuse this method.

E1.justification: Both versions use MADLAD-400 and NLLB for training and FLORES, XNLI, XCOPA, Belebele and MMMLU for evaluation across the same 11 languages. The All group combines already covered languages; LLaMA changes the model configuration rather than dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 10–11 introduce unadapted LLaMA2-7B as the reference for the new LLaMA adaptation experiments. The original Mistral, ZeTT, OFA and FOCUS comparisons remain intact, with no additional competing vocabulary-adaptation algorithm.

E3.justification: Section 5.2 revises the stated adapter-training budget from 3.5B to 2.5B tokens, without establishing that the original experiments were rerun. Appendix F adds an 11-language model trained on 5.5B tokens and LLaMA2-7B experiments. Figure 5 adds alpha=0.2 and replaces individual-language examples with group averages; the main metrics and prompting protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The auxiliary-loss analysis expands from alpha values 0 and 0.1 on Estonian/Greek examples to three values and four-language group averages. Appendix F adds All-versus-Multi scalability and cross-backbone analyses, while Appendix D adds computational profiling. The original script-grouping analysis is retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. v2 adds a caution about interpreting small metric differences, but no uncertainty-estimation procedure. Figure 5 averages languages rather than repeated runs.

E6.justification: Tables 2–8 are unchanged, but Tables 10–11 add extensive All-group and LLaMA results, and Figure 6 and Appendix D add token-count and computational results. Revised Figure 5 reports milder Latin auxiliary-loss penalties under changed aggregation. Some new Figure 3b labels conflict with retained tables: Russian-to-English is labeled -1.6%, versus -3.33% in Table 3.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and Equations 1–4 remain unchanged, with no added theorem or proof. The new discussion of convex-hull initialization cites prior work, while the linear-combination limitation is a qualitative hypothesis rather than a new formal result.

C1.justification: The principal method, language-benefit and downstream-translation claims remain. The auxiliary-loss finding is qualified and de-emphasized: v1's introduction says preserving overlapping embeddings is not useful for Latin languages, whereas v2 Appendix A describes omitting the loss as only slightly better or comparable.

C2.justification: Appendix B adds a hypothesized explanation for Korean failures involving token decomposition and byte fallbacks. Appendix C discusses noisy training data, metric domain dependence, missing document context and the interpretation of small score differences. v2 also moderates the auxiliary-loss interpretation and discusses evidence for scalability and backbone generalization.

D1.justification: Appendices C–D newly disclose batch size 128, gradient accumulation, 38k update steps, FLOP profiling and baseline implementation sources. Appendix F supplies an All-group model link and additional training information. Most existing hardware and optimization details are retained; these additions chiefly improve documentation.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds explicit positioning around learning linear combinations of embeddings and prior convex-hull initialization arguments. Appendices A and C substantially expand discussion and citations concerning adaptation regularization, web-corpus noise, translation metrics, context and statistical interpretation.

P1.justification: v2 edits the introduction and conclusion, expands Background into Background and Motivation, separates full-weight fine-tuning into a subsection and moves the auxiliary-loss discussion into Appendix A. The main narrative remains recognizable. Author information, publication headers and acknowledgements also change.

P2.justification: Figures 2–4 gain numerical annotations; Figure 3 explicitly labels negative changes and expands token-count axes to display Greek's full count. Figure 5 is redesigned and relocated. Tables 10–11 and Figure 6 are added, while Figure 1, Table 2 and the related-work table receive placement or presentation changes.

improvement.justification: The All-language and LLaMA experiments provide useful additional support for scalability and transfer beyond Mistral. Broader auxiliary-loss analysis, explicit limitations and computational disclosures improve assessability. These gains are tempered by the unexplained training-budget revision and discrepancies between new Figure 3 labels and retained tables. The evidence supports a limited overall improvement.
